message.content: Handlers return a mode/data reply hash rather than a bare status string to enforce a strict, machine-readable contract that eliminates ambiguity in response parsing. A bare status string would force every caller to implement fragile string-parsing logic that must account for all possible status codes, while a hash-based reply provides an explicit schema where the `mode` field dictates the shape of the `data` payload, enabling compile-time validation, automatic type coercion, and consistent error propagation. This design also future-proofs the protocol: new response fields can be added to the hash structure without breaking existing callers, and the separation of mode and data allows handlers to encode rich contextual information (e.g., version tags, metadata, or structured error details) without bloating the status string itself.
